# 3 Ways to Install DataForSEO MCP With Claude Code

[DataForSEO Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://dataforseo.com/model-context-protocol) integration with [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) allows for seamless access to DataForSEO’s comprehensive SEO data suite directly from your command line. In this guide we’ll cover three MCP installation methods to get you up and running in no time.

#### Prerequisites

Before installing DataForSEO MCP, make sure you have:

- Node.js (version 18 or higher) installed;
- Claude Code installed globally (check [Anthropic docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) for details);
- DataForSEO account with API credentials [(API login and password)](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access);
- Your Anthropic API key is configured with Claude Code.

#### Method 1: Add Remote MCP Server

The easiest way is to install MCP as a remote server:

```
claude mcp add --header "Authorization: Basic <basic_auth_token>" --transport http dfs-mcp https://mcp.dataforseo.com/http
```

As the `<basic_auth_token>`, specify your DataForSEO API credentials, encoded in the [Base64 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base64). You can find your API credentials in the [API Access](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access) tab of your DataForSEO account.

![Screenshot 2025 09 05 at 17.23.29](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Screenshot-2025-09-05-at-17.23.29.png)

#### Method 2: Add Local MCP Server From the NPM Repository

If you prefer to keep MCP servers locally, you can add DataForSEO MCP to your system from the NPM repository:

```
claude mcp add dfs-mcp --env DATAFORSEO_USERNAME=<api_username> --env DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD=<api_password> -- npx -y dataforseo-mcp-server
```

Instead of `<api_username>` and `<api_password>` input your API login and API password from the [API Access](https://app.dataforseo.com/api-access) tab of your DataForSEO account.

![Screenshot 2025 09 05 at 18.08.08](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Screenshot-2025-09-05-at-18.08.08.png)

If you’re using Windows, the most reliable approach is to edit the config file directly. The `mcpServers` object in `.claude.json` contains all MCP configurations, with each tool having its own named entry.

Open `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json` (e.g. `C:\Users\YourName\.claude.json`) and add this to the `mcpServers` object:

```
{
  "dfs-mcp": {
    "type": "stdio",
    "command": "cmd",
    "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "dataforseo-mcp-server"],
    "env": {
      "DATAFORSEO_USERNAME": "api_username",
      "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD": "api_password"
    }
  }
}
```

#### Method 3: Add Local MCP Server With Custom Changes

If you need to make certain changes to DataForSEO MCP server and then make these changes work in Claude Code, you can add MCP server locally with custom changes.

```
claude mcp add dfs-mcp --env DATAFORSEO_USERNAME=<api_username> --env DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD=<api_password> -- node <path_to_changed_repository>\\mcp-server-typescript\\build\\main\\main\\index.js
```

![Screenshot 2025 09 05 at 19.01.33](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Screenshot-2025-09-05-at-19.01.33.png)

#### Verification

After installation, it’ll be a good idea to verify that DataForSEO MCP is working correctly with the following command:

```
claude test-mcp dataforseo
```

You should see a confirmation message indicating successful connection to DataForSEO APIs. If something went wrong, Claude Code will also display troubleshooting tips.

![Screenshot 2025 09 05 at 19.19.42](https://dataforseo.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Screenshot-2025-09-05-at-19.19.42.png)
